chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Briggs as Sissle's straw boss
summary: Because Sissle was not a musician, he hired Briggs to run rehearsals, call the music, set tempos and handle the floor shows, with players like Buster Bailey.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Was he a trained musician?
No, Sissle was not a musician, no.
Right.
He was a singer, he was an actor. That's why he hired me.
Because you were the straw boss on the band; is that right?
Yes, uh huh.
Briggs
I see. So he brought you in to be straw boss?
Yes.
I see. Right. And you would run the rehearsals and --
And everything, and take care of the floor shows, and everything else.
So he had to pay you pretty well, because you were really running the band.
But he made me the proposition, I didn't ask for the proposition.
Right.

He said, 'I'll pay you so and so.' He said, 'You'll have to do so and so and so and so.' 'I'll come in, and you're in charge of the orchestra.' 'You start the orchestra whether I'm there or not, you just go ahead and run the orchestra.'
Briggs 212
"And I want you to take care of the floor show. Floor shows and everything else." "And you call the music, and every set you call, and I should have at least one number to sing."
So he wouldn't even be out on the stand until it was time for him to sing?
Yes, but he was very conscientious.
But did he conduct at all?
No, he did the best that he could.
Probably waved the stick, a little.
Yes.
But you were setting tempos and counting the band off.
Yeh, sure.
I see.
Well, we had men like
Briggs
Buster Bailey, and we had a terrific bass player, I don't know whether you've heard of him, Bass Edwards.
Sure.
Yeh. He smoked one of those great big cigars, playing with this cigar --
He was playing tuba then.
Tuba, tuba, yes, sure.
With a cigar while he was playing tuba?
